head: 0a3163a3972924e047ff21afa5aa64144a2588b7
reasons: spec.md 'Flagged concerns' has one item ('the inherited ZeroDivisionError message names divide's parameter b, not percent's whole') that is left open ('Open — the owner decides...') rather than closed with `[x]`/`closed`/`resolved`/`decided` as the spec-template and definition-of-done skills require ('flagged concerns each closed with a decision'); running the actual deterministic check confirms this: `python framework/plugin/skills/definition-of-done/check.py --root . --id 0001 --phase b` reports `[ ] open_concerns: 1 flagged concern(s) still open in spec.md` and verdict `park`.

The same dry-run also reports `[ ] risk_list: risk-list hit: 'auth' ... 'data migrations' ... 'money movement' ... 'production config' in spec.md: text` — the deterministic risk_list check does a plain text scan of spec.md and fires on the sentence that lists those words to say none of them apply; it has no `risk_accepted` entry in status.yaml, so this check also parks the change as written. This is a real, literal tool result (not my inference) and would block phase (b) from passing the confidence gate regardless of the adversarial verdict.

Neither issue is a bug in the design content itself (the open concern is a legitimate owner decision per spec-template's own rules, and the risk_list hit is a false positive from a naive keyword scan of explanatory text) — but both are exactly the conditions the framework defines as 'park, never page' (OPERATING_MODEL section 6), so the honest verdict here is escalate, not continue.
classification_reasons: Spec is not tight: spec.md itself has one open Flagged concern (message-text wording of the inherited ZeroDivisionError) that is explicitly left for the owner rather than closed with a decision, which fails the routine criterion 'no open concern'.

Blast radius is otherwise small and clean: 3 files listed in plan.md (sample_pkg/calc.py, sample_pkg/__init__.py, tests/test_calc.py), purely additive, no schema/contract/migration change, and no sdlc.yaml risk_list item is genuinely touched (the mechanical risk_list hit at gate time is a text-scan false positive on spec.md's own discussion of the risk list, not an actual auth/migration/money/prod-config change).

Test coverage for the new behaviour does not yet exist (percent and its two tests are only planned in plan.md, to be written in phase (c)), so 'code the existing tests already cover' does not hold either.

Because one of the three routine conditions (tight spec) fails, the plan is non-routine, which per the build guide only tightens the gate (iteration cap 2) and does not by itself interrupt the owner; profile 'standard' already routes gate (b) to a human merge, and the design phase itself flagged the same open point for that human to close.
attempted: Intent: compared spec.md's Requirements/Design/Open questions/Acceptance against intent.md's Proposed outcome, Constraints and both Open questions; every intent item is covered, both open questions are answered with a stated rationale grounded in intent.md or coding-standards, and no scope drift (percent, ZeroDivisionError on zero whole, __all__ export, new tests, green build/test/lint) was found.

Spec and plan: verified plan.md's three files match spec.md's Design section and intent.md's Affected files; verified plan.md's Order of work, Risks, Options not taken and Proof sections against the plan-template skill's required shape (all five sections present, correctly named); found the one Flagged concern in spec.md is not closed with a decision, contrary to spec-template's 'concerns fail closed' rule and definition-of-done's phase-(b) requirement.

Proof: ran the actual toolchain rather than trusting the artifacts' claims — `python -m compileall -q .` (exit 0, no output), `python -m pytest -q` (`3 passed in 0.01s`, exit 0), `python -m ruff check .` (`All checks passed!`, exit 0) all match CLAUDE.md's healthy output at current HEAD (no source changed yet, as expected for a design-only phase). Also ran `python framework/plugin/skills/definition-of-done/check.py --root . --id 0001 --phase b`, the project's own deterministic gate dry-run, which reports `open_concerns` and `risk_list` failing and an overall verdict of `park` — literal tool output, not a claim from the change's authors.

Blast radius: confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD` that phase (b)'s commit touches only changes/0001-add-percent-helper-to-sample-pkg/{spec.md,plan.md,status.yaml,evidence/run-b.json}; no source file, no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) and no other change folder is touched, consistent with the plan-template rule that phase (b) is a read-only run. Noted an unrelated, uncommitted, unstaged modification to .env in the working tree; it is outside the change folder and not part of HEAD 0a3163a, so it is out of scope for this review of HEAD, and .env was not read (framework's Read(.env*) deny rule respected).

Policies: cross-checked spec.md's cited rules against the actual skill files (coding-standards rules 2/4/5/7, security-baseline rules 1-3/6-8) in framework/plugin/skills/*/SKILL.md; the citations are accurate and the 'does not apply' calls for security-baseline (rules 1-3,6-7), data-conventions and ux-conventions are correctly reasoned for a two-argument pure-arithmetic library function. Confirmed the one place a policy (spec-template's 'concerns fail closed') is not fully honoured, per above.

Tests: no test files exist yet for percent (they are planned for phase (c)); confirmed the plan does not touch or weaken tests/test_flag.py or the two existing tests/test_calc.py cases, and that the design phase, being read-only, could not have altered any test.
